finding: Each per-set sky flat carries a DIFFERENT sky gradient, and the difference grows monotonically through the night. Dividing lights by a flat that contains sky stamps the inverse of that sky onto the OBJECT.
instrument: Siril only — `idiv` of one flat by another (which CANCELS the optical response exactly: same lens, focal, aperture, focus, night), then `crop` + `stat` medians. No in-house pixel maths; this record only reports what Siril printed.
why_division_is_the_right_operator: A flat is V x (1+g): optical response times whatever sky was baked in. flat_i / flat_j = (1+g_i)/(1+g_j) — V divides out identically, so the ratio isolates the sky term with no model, no fit and no assumption.

measured_corner_spread_of_the_ratio_pct._GEOMETRY_UNSTATED: these five figures declare no box geometry and do not reproduce from the surviving artifacts at box 400 / margin 200. Use remeasured_2026_08_06_at_a_STATED_geometry instead; these are kept as the historical record.

additivity: adjacent gaps sum to the wide gaps: 7.11+10.56=17.67 vs 18.55 measured; 7.11+10.56+12.07=29.74 vs 31.68 measured. A monotonically evolving term, not a fixed optical one.  [SUPERSEDED — see additivity_RECHECKED_and_it_STANDS: the sums hold, on corrected numbers, more tightly than stated here.]
spatial_form: smooth monotonic diagonal tilt, 5x5 grid on flat01/flat03: -8.05% at one corner to +9.70% at the opposite, 19.31% peak-to-peak, no structure beyond the tilt at this sampling.

ruled_out.vignetting_or_any_optical_term: CANCELS by construction in a ratio of two flats from the same lens/focal/aperture/night. This is why the ratio was used instead of comparing flats to a model.
ruled_out.frame_count: flat02/flat03 is 500 vs 500 frames — IDENTICAL counts — and still shows 10.56%. Counts cannot produce it.
ruled_out.dew: dew's recorded signature (docs/dead-ends.md, july23) is a growing star halo with rising FWHM AND a terminal nstars CRASH of 13-16%. Here nstars RISES across the night (1166 -> 1256, +8%) while FWHM creeps 2.334 -> 2.576 px. Rising star count is the opposite of dew.
ruled_out.sky_getting_brighter: background level is FLAT across all four sets (bg16 median 1117 / 1115 / 1117 / 1117). The sky did not brighten; its GRADIENT changed direction and magnitude. That is a geometry change, not a brightness change.
ruled_out.the_lens_distortion_model: identical pinned model for all four sets, asserted per set by lens_preflight against scripts/darktable/lens_models.json.

NOT_ruled_out_and_is_the_likely_source: MOONLIGHT and airmass. july31 was shot under a 93.7% moon. A horizon-fixed gradient is exactly what a bright moon plus airmass produces, and it sits STILL on the sensor of a fixed mount while the sky drifts past — so it cannot reject out of a median of un-registered lights. That is the documented mechanism in docs/dead-ends.md. IMPORTANT: the moon is the SOURCE of the gradient, not the defect. The defect is that a flat built from those same lights absorbs it and division then stamps its inverse onto the object. No processing removes moonlight; a flat that does not contain it would not tilt the object.
predicted_consequence_UNTESTED: Each set's object is modulated by 1/(1+g_i) with a DIFFERENT g_i. Registered to sky and combined, the four different multiplicative tilts do not cancel — they leave a residual that is neither sky nor object. This is the hypothesis for both the linear corner-spread trend (0.40/0.50/1.03/1.17% for sets 01-04 in capture order) and any local dullness in the combined frame. STATED AS A HYPOTHESIS. The controlled test is in AUDIT_FLAT_GRADIENT_PROMPT.md.
instrument_CORRECTED_2026_08_06: The `instrument` field below is WRONG and is kept only to show what it said. It states '`idiv` of one flat by another'. The two surviving artifacts prove otherwise: a `fdiv <B> 0.5` rebuild reproduces flatratio_set-01_over_set-03 to Mean 31127.9 / Median 30998.7 / Max 45126.4 and flatratio_set-01_over_set-04 to 31229.9 / 30963.0 / 65535.0 — every figure exact — while a plain `idiv` of the same md5-verified flats gives Median 61997.5, i.e. EXACTLY 2.0000x the artifact. So a 0.5 scalar was applied and never written down. That undocumented choice is what SAVED this measurement (see idiv_clipping below); reproducing the record as WRITTEN would understate every figure by up to 9.1 points.

idiv_clipping_the_trap_this_record_ESCAP.mechanism: Siril `idiv` clips at 1.0 silently; the tell is a whole-frame `stat` printing Max exactly 65535.0. A ratio of two comparable flats sits near 1.0, so a large fraction of the frame lands past the clip.

severity_if_this_record_HAD_used_idiv_as.note: corner spread, box 400 / margin 200, unclipped `fdiv` leg vs plain `idiv` leg, same flats, same geometry
severity_if_this_record_HAD_used_idiv_as.worst_case: -9.128 points on a 27.843-point measurement = 33% understated. flat03/flat04's idiv leg has a whole-frame MEDIAN of exactly 65535.0, i.e. more than half the frame is at the clip.
severity_if_this_record_HAD_used_idiv_as.why_the_fdiv_leg_is_trusted: `fdiv 0.25` and `fdiv 0.5` agree exactly after rescaling on all five pairs (e.g. 01/04 median 15481.5 x2 = 30963.0), so no scale-dependent truncation is moving the medians. Where Max still reads 65535.0 at both scalars (03/04, 01/04) the cause is a genuine divide-by-near-zero spike, not bulk clipping — medians are unaffected.

remeasured_2026_08_06_at_a_STATED_geomet.why: the original corner spreads state no box geometry and are therefore not reproducible. Measured directly on the two SURVIVING artifacts, the recorded values do not reproduce at box 400 / margin 200 — the artifact for 01/03 reads 17.127 against a recorded 18.55, and 01/04 reads 27.843 against 31.68. The artifacts are byte-present and were measured directly, so the difference is GEOMETRY, not the data.

remeasured_2026_08_06_at_a_STATED_geomet.surviving_artifacts_reproduce_exactly: flatratio_set-01_over_set-03 measures 17.127 and my fdiv rebuild measures 17.127; flatratio_set-01_over_set-04 measures 27.843 and my rebuild measures 27.843. The instrument reproduces the artifacts to three decimals.

additivity_RECHECKED_and_it_STANDS.verdict: the additivity claim — and the conclusion it carries, 'a monotonically evolving term, not a fixed optical one' — SURVIVES the correction and is BETTER supported by the corrected numbers than by the recorded ones (the record's own figures were 5% and 6.5% apart; corrected they are 0.6% and 2.6% on corner spread, 0.9% and 1.1% on the ramp slope). The RAMP SLOPE is the more additive measure, consistent with docs/dead-ends.md preferring it over a four-corner metric.
additivity_RECHECKED_and_it_STANDS.what_changed_and_what_did_not: the NUMBERS move (every recorded figure is 0.3-3.8 points high at box 400/margin 200) and the stated INSTRUMENT was wrong. The FINDING is unaffected.
